name: Dusty moss
lede: Dusty moss is a muted sage green, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Usu'ao, whose name literally means "pale blue."

sections.title: A "pale blue" that reads as green
sections.body:
Usu'ao (薄青) is listed in the Wikipedia catalog of Japan's traditional colors with the literal meaning "pale blue" [1]. On today's screens the swatch reads as a muted sage green, not blue; older Japanese color vocabulary grouped blue and green more loosely than modern English does, and the name has outlasted that shift [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[celadon-green]] and [[asphodel-green]], at 2.7 and 3.4 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 305 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.3 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest match is a Buddhist painting of Mahamayuri Vidyaraja dated to 916, where it covers about a quarter of the image, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. The rate is highest in a sample of 258 paintings from the 1740s, more than three and a half times the archive's overall rate for that decade [2]. It is unusually common among painters working in the late 1800s sampled in our archive, including Gustav Klimt, Camille Pissarro, Paul Cézanne, Berthe Morisot and Vincent van Gogh [2]. It is also disproportionately present in paintings from Nepal, Austria, Tibet and India [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
